questions.question:
**Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.**

The new policy has had A. a positive affect on the company's C. bottom line, but it has D. also caused some negative publicity.

options.text: a positive affect on the company's

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the misuse of the word "**affect**" instead of "**effect**."
 
• In this context, we need a noun to follow the adjective "positive." "**Effect**" is a noun meaning a result or consequence, whereas "**affect**" is primarily a verb meaning to influence.
 
• The phrase should be "**a positive effect on**," which correctly identifies the impact the policy had on the company.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part A** (Option 2) of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The new policy has had a positive **effect** on the company's bottom line, but it has also caused some negative publicity."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "The new policy has had" **– This part uses the present perfect tense correctly to describe an action that began in the past and continues to have relevance.
 
• **Option 3: "bottom line, but it has"** – This part is correct; "bottom line" is a standard business term for net income, and the conjunction "but" properly introduces the contrast.
 
• **Option 4: "also caused some negative publicity"** – This part is grammatically sound and correctly completes the second half of the contrast.
 
• **Affect vs. Effect:** A common mnemonic is **RAVEN**: **R**emember **A**ffect **V**erb **E**ffect **N**oun.

questions.question:
**Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.**

A. The painting B. is the most unique C. of all the pieces D. in the gallery.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the comparative modifier "**most**" with the word "**unique**."
 
• "Unique" is an **absolute adjective**, meaning it describes a state that cannot be intensified or compared. Something is either unique (the only one of its kind) or it is not.
 
• Using "most unique," "very unique," or "more unique" is considered a logical and grammatical error in formal English because you cannot be "more" of the only one.
 
• The correct phrase should simply be "**is unique**" or "**is the most unusual**" if a comparison is intended.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The painting **is unique** of all the pieces in the gallery."* (Or: *"The painting is the most **remarkable**..."*)

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "The painting" **– This is the subject of the sentence and is grammatically correct.
 
• **Option 3: "of all the pieces"** – This prepositional phrase is used correctly to define the group being discussed.
 
• **Option 4: "in the gallery"** – This correctly identifies the location and contains no errors.
 
• **Absolute Adjectives:** Other examples include *dead, square, essential,* and *infinite*. You wouldn't typically say something is "very dead" or "more infinite."

questions.question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives:

Sujit said, "Can you pass me the chilli sauce please?"

options.text: Sujit requested if he could pass him the chilli sauce please.
Sujit requested if he can pass him the chilli sauce please.
Sujit requested if he can pass him the chilli sauce.
Sujit requested if he could pass him the chilli sauce.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** Sujit said, "Can you pass me the chilli sauce please?"
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• The word "please" indicates a request. Therefore, the reporting verb **"said"** is converted to **"requested"**.
 
 
 
• **"Can" becomes "could":**
 
 
• When the reporting verb is in the past tense ("said/requested"), the modal verb **"can"** must be changed to its past form **"could"** in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Pronoun change:**
 
 
• The first-person pronoun **"me"** refers to the speaker (Sujit), so it changes to the third-person **"him"**.
 
 
 
• **Removal of "Please":**
 
 
• In indirect speech, the word **"please"** is omitted because the sense of requesting is already conveyed by the reporting verb "requested."
 
 
 
 
 
• **Structure:** Since the direct speech is a Yes/No question, we use the conjunction **"if"** or **"whether"** to join the reporting clause and the reported speech.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Sujit requested if he could pass him the chilli sauce."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Sujit requested if he could pass him the chilli sauce please." 

 
 
• Incorrect because it redundantly includes the word "please" at the end.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "Sujit requested if he can pass him the chilli sauce please." 
 
 
• Incorrect because "can" is not changed to "could" and it retains "please."
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "Sujit requested if he can pass him the chilli sauce." 
 
 
• Incorrect because the modal verb "can" remains in the present tense, which does not match the past tense reporting verb.

questions.question:
**Change the following sentence into the Active form.**

The decision will have been announced before the meeting concludes.

options.text: Someone will announce the decision before the meeting concludes.
They will have announced the decision before the meeting concludes.
The decision will be announced before the meeting concludes.
The meeting will have announced the decision.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tense Identification:** The original sentence "will have been announced" is in the **Future Perfect Passive** voice.
 
• **Active Voice Rule:** To convert Future Perfect Passive to Active, the structure changes from "will have been + V3" to "**will have + V3**".
 
• **Subject Placement:** Since the passive sentence does not specify who is announcing the decision, a generic subject like "They" or "Someone" is used in the active voice.
 
• **Object Placement:** The subject of the passive sentence ("The decision") becomes the object of the active sentence.
 
• **Conjunctions:** The phrase "before the meeting concludes" remains unchanged as it provides the time context for the action.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"They will have announced the decision before the meeting concludes."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Someone will announce..." changes the tense to Future Simple, which alters the original meaning of a completed action in the future.
 
• **Option 3:** "The decision will be announced..." is still in the passive voice and changes the tense to Future Simple Passive.
 
• **Option 4:** "The meeting will have announced..." is logically incorrect as it implies the meeting itself is performing the action of announcing.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.**

He said, "The train will leave in ten minutes."

options.text: He said that the train would leave in ten minutes.
He said that the train will leave in ten minutes.
He said that the train left in ten minutes.
He said that the train was leaving in ten minutes.

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** He said, "The train will leave in ten minutes."
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:**
 
 
• The reporting verb **"said"** remains **"said"** in indirect speech because it is not followed by an object (e.g., "said to me").
 
 
 
• **Conjunction:**
 
 
• The comma and quotation marks are removed and replaced by the conjunction **"that"** to connect the reporting clause with the reported speech.
 
 
 
• **Tense Change (Will to Would):**
 
 
• Since the reporting verb is in the past tense ("said"), the future tense modal **"will"** must be changed to its past equivalent, **"would"**.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Structure:** The sentence follows the standard rule for assertive sentences where the tense shifts backward when the reporting verb is in the past.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He said that the train would leave in ten minutes."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "He said that the train will leave in ten minutes." 

 
 
• Incorrect because it fails to change the modal "will" to "would," which is necessary when the reporting verb is in the past.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "He said that the train left in ten minutes." 
 
 
• Incorrect because "will leave" (future) is incorrectly changed to "left" (simple past), which alters the original meaning.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "He said that the train was leaving in ten minutes." 
 
 
• Incorrect because it changes the tense to past continuous, which does not accurately reflect the simple future "will leave."

questions.question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

The man was **effected by **the remarks made by his peers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**affected by**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The word "**affected**" is the correct past tense of the verb "**affect**," which means to influence or impact.
 
• The word "**effected**" is incorrect here as it means "to bring about" or "to cause," which does not fit the context of the sentence.
 
• The preposition "**by**" is used to indicate the agent or cause of an action, making "**affected by**" the correct choice.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"The man was **affected by**__ the remarks made by his peers."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "affected with"** is incorrect because "with" does not fit the context of the sentence.
 
• **Option 2: "effected with"** is incorrect because "effected" is not the correct verb to indicate being influenced by something.
 
• **Option 4: "effected to"** is incorrect as "effected" is used in the sense of causing something to happen, not being influenced.
</ul

questions.question:
**Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:**

The cat drank all the milk.

options.text: All the milk was drunk by the cat.
All the milk is drunk by the cat.
All the milk has been drunk by the cat.
All the milk had been drunk by the cat.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tense Identification:** The original sentence "The cat **drank** all the milk" is in the **Simple Past** tense.
 
• **Passive Voice Rule:** To convert Simple Past to Passive, the structure used is "**was/were + past participle (V3)**".
 
• **Subject-Object Swap:** The object of the active sentence ("all the milk") becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• **Verb Conversion:** The past tense "drank" changes to "was drunk" because "milk" is an uncountable (singular) noun.
 
• **Agent:** The original subject "the cat" is added at the end, preceded by the preposition "by."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"All the milk was drunk by the cat."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "is drunk" is in the Simple Present Passive, which changes the timing of the action.
 
• **Option 3:** "has been drunk" is in the Present Perfect Passive, which implies a connection to the present.
 
• **Option 4:** "had been drunk" is in the Past Perfect Passive, used for actions completed before another past action.

• **Subject-Verb Agreement:** Because "All employees" is plural, the auxiliary verb must be "**have**" (not "has").
 
• **Maintaining Meaning:** Option 1 preserves the exact tense and meaning of the original active sentence while shifting the focus to the employees.

The politician declared that he would not be swayed by the opposition's baseless accusations which were aimed at destabilizing the government that had been working for the welfare of the country for years.

"He would not be swayed by the opposition's baseless accusations which were aimed at destabilizing the government that had been working for the welfare of the country for years," the politician declared.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The politician declared that he would not be swayed by the opposition's baseless accusations which were aimed at destabilizing the government that had been working for the welfare of the country for years.
 
• **Key Conversions from Indirect to Direct:**
 
 
• **Pronoun change:**
 
 
• The third-person **"he"** in indirect speech refers to the politician, so it must change to the first-person **"I"** in direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Tense Change (Back-shifting Reversed):**
 
 
• **"would"** changes back to **"will"** (future).
 
• **"were aimed"** (simple past) changes back to **"are aimed"** (simple present).
 
• **"had been working"** (past perfect continuous) changes back to **"has been working"** (present perfect continuous).
 
 
 
• **Conjunction Removal:**
 
 
• The conjunction **"that"** is removed and replaced by a comma and quotation marks to introduce the direct words of the speaker.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Structure:** When converting back to direct speech, the tenses must move forward (e.g., past to present) to reflect the original moment the politician spoke.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"“I will not be swayed by the opposition's baseless accusations which are aimed at destabilizing the government that has been working for the welfare of the country for years,” the politician declared."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Incorrect because it fails to change "were aimed" and "had been working" back to their present forms, creating a tense mismatch within the direct quote.
 
• **Option 2:** Incorrect because it retains "would" instead of "will" and uses the past continuous "was working" incorrectly.
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect because it keeps the pronoun in the third-person ("He") and maintains past tenses ("would," "were," "had been"), which is not the standard format for direct speech.

questions.question:
Identify the **voice** (active or passive) and the **tense** of the verb in the sentence:

"Many healthcare institutions follow strict guidelines to ensure that hazardous waste is not mixed with general waste."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sentence:** "Many healthcare institutions follow strict guidelines to ensure that hazardous waste is not mixed with general waste."
 
• **Voice Identification:**
 
 
• The subject **"Many healthcare institutions"** performs the action **"follow"**.
 
• Since the subject is doing the action, the sentence is in the **Active Voice**.
 
 
 
• **Tense Identification:**
 
 
• The verb **"follow"** is in its base form used with a plural subject.
 
• This indicates the **Simple Present Tense**, which describes general truths or habitual actions.
 
 
 
• **Additional Clause Explanation:**
 
 
• The clause **"hazardous waste is not mixed with general waste"** is in the **passive voice**, but it is only a subordinate clause.
 
• The question focuses on the **main verb of the sentence**, which is **"follow"** (active voice, simple present).
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Identification:** *Active voice, simple present.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Passive voice, simple past

 
 
• Incorrect because the verb **"follow"** is not in passive voice and not in past tense.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** Active voice, present perfect
 
 
• Incorrect because present perfect would require **"have followed"**, which is not used in the sentence.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** Passive voice, present continuous
 
 
• Incorrect because present continuous passive would be **"are being followed"**, which is not present in the sentence.

questions.question:
Identify the** part of speech** of the word **"properly" **in the sentence:

"If not handled and disposed of properly, this waste can pose serious risks to human health and the environment."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2** i.e '**Adverb**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"properly"** modifies the verbs **"handled"** and **"disposed"** by explaining *how* the actions were performed, which is a characteristic of an adverb.
 
• **Adverbs often **answer the questions how, when, where, and to what extent. In this case, "properly" is answering "how" the waste should be handled and disposed of.
 
• The word **"properly"** ends in -ly, which is a common suffix for adverbs, although not all words ending in -ly are adverbs.
 
• **Adverbs can modify **verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs, further specifying or qualifying the action or characteristic they are describing.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adjective: **An adjective modifies or describes a noun or pronoun. In the given sentence, "properly" does not describe a noun, so it is not an adjective.
 
• **Preposition: **A preposition shows the relationship between words (e.g., in, on, at). "Properly" does not function as a preposition here.
 
• **Pronoun: **A pronoun replaces a noun (e.g., he, she, it). "Properly" is not replacing a noun, so it is not a pronoun.

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.text: Medical waste management is essential to protect health and environment
Hospitals can mix all waste together
Incineration is the only method of disposal

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 1) Medical waste is not harmful***

 
 
• This **cannot be inferred** from the passage. The passage clearly states that medical waste can pose serious risks to human health and the environment if not managed properly.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2) Medical waste management is essential to protect health and environment***
 
 
• This **is the main idea** of the passage. It emphasizes the importance of proper medical waste management to safeguard both human health and the environment.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3) Hospitals can mix all waste together***
 
 
• This **cannot be inferred**. The passage highlights that healthcare institutions follow strict guidelines to ensure hazardous waste is not mixed with general waste.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4) Incineration is the only method of disposal***
 
 
• This **cannot be inferred**. The passage mentions multiple methods such as incineration, chemical treatment, and secure landfills.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: Incorrect because the passage states medical waste is harmful if not managed properly.
 
• **Option 3**: Incorrect because hospitals must separate hazardous waste from general waste.
 
• **Option 4**: Incorrect because incineration is not the only method; chemical treatment and secure landfills are also mentioned.

questions.question: What term describes the assumption of something as true without proof?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **3) Presumption**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Presumption"** means the act of assuming something to be true without proof or evidence. (अनुमान)
 
 
• **Example:** His presumption that everyone would agree with his plan turned out to be wrong.
 
 
• **"Presumption"** often implies a belief or acceptance of something as likely or true, even though it hasn't been confirmed. (अधिकार मान लेना)
 
 
• **Example:** The court operates on the presumption of innocence until proven guilty.
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **3) Presumption**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Hypothesis** (परिकल्पना): A proposed explanation made on the basis of limited evidence as a starting point for further investigation.
 
 
• **Example:** The scientist proposed a hypothesis to explain the unusual weather patterns.
 
 
 
• **Inference** (निष्कर्ष): A conclusion reached on the basis of evidence and reasoning.
 
 
• **Example:** Based on the evidence, the detective made an inference about the suspect's whereabouts.
 
 
 
• **Conclusion** (निष्कर्ष): The end or finish of an event or process; a judgment or decision reached by reasoning.
 
 
• **Example:** After hours of debate, the committee reached a conclusion on the matter.
